short: A fifth-generation American stealth tactical fighter emphasizing air superiority.
full:
The Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor achieved initial operational capability in December 2005, introducing the fifth generation of jet fighters. It combined stealth, supercruise — the ability to sustain supersonic flight without afterburners — and highly integrated avionics to ensure absolute air dominance. Its thrust-vectoring engines also granted it exceptional maneuverability in close-range combat.

Federal law prohibited the export of the F-22 to protect its classified stealth technology, leaving the United States as its sole operator. Production was halted at one hundred and eighty-seven operational aircraft due to high costs and the lack of comparable adversary fighters at the time. It made its combat debut in 2014, conducting strikes against Islamic State targets in Syria.
